evals.name: laravel-ticket-checkout
evals.prompt: I'm building event ticket checkout in our Laravel 11 app and want customers to pay with EcoCash using the EcoCash Instant Payment (EIP) API - we have sandbox credentials from developers.ecocash.co.zw. Write the service class, the config, and a controller with two endpoints: one that starts payment for an order, and one the frontend polls to get the result. Save the files.
evals.expected_output: A Laravel service, config and controller that send the exact EIP charge body, keep the base path, save a unique clientCorrelator before charging, poll with the lookup endpoint and fulfil only on status SUCCESS.

assertions.text: The charge body uses the exact keys charginginformation (all lowercase), chargeMetaData and terminalID
The charge is POSTed to /transactions/amount/ (trailing slash) under the base URL https://developers.ecocash.co.zw/sandbox/payment/v1 without dropping /sandbox/payment/v1
The polling endpoint uses GET /{endUserId}/transactions/amount/{clientCorrelator}
A new unique clientCorrelator is generated per payment and stored on the order before or with the charge request
The code treats the charge's HTTP 200 as accepted/pending and marks the order paid only when the returned status is SUCCESS
A timeout or network error does not trigger a second charge; the code or its notes say to look the payment up instead
Credentials and merchantPin come from config/env, not hard-coded in the service

evals.name: broken-refund-payload
evals.expected_output: findings.md listing every defect with its cause, and a refund.json that fixes them.

assertions.text: Identifies chargingInformation must be charginginformation (all lowercase)
Identifies chargeMetadata must be chargeMetaData and terminalId must be terminalID
Identifies the missing originalEcocashReference (the original charge's EcoCash reference/transactionId)
Says the hard-coded/reused clientCorrelator REF-001 must be a new unique value
Flags that the refund amount 25 exceeds the original 20 (E012/422)
Explains the 409 as the original charge not being SUCCESS (HTTP 200 on the charge only meant accepted) or already refunded
Addresses tranType: says the documentation specifies REF/REV while the portal's samples/Playground send MER, without presenting one as confirmed
refund.json passes `eip_cli.py lint` with no errors
refund.json contains only documented EIP fields: `eip_cli.py lint` reports no 'not a documented EIP field' warnings

evals.name: dotnet-404-base-path
evals.expected_output: fix.md explaining that the leading-slash paths drop /sandbox/payment/v1 and that the status field is status, with corrected C#.

assertions.text: Explains that a leading-slash relative path replaces the BaseAddress path, so /sandbox/payment/v1 is dropped (requests go to /transactions/amount/ at the host root)
Fix: BaseAddress ending with / and paths without a leading slash (e.g. "transactions/amount/"), or full absolute URLs
Keeps the trailing slash on transactions/amount/ (does not remove it)
Identifies that the documented response field is status (transactionStatus comes from the portal's SDK samples) and reads status, optionally with fallbacks
Notes that a 200 on the charge means accepted/PENDING, not paid
